author: sonnet
label: climb-03-01
changes: Added a two-sentence summary and a short terms block at the top (raw token, live link, link format with APP_BASE_URL) so the link contents are clear.
Added trim and lowercase email lookup in the request flow and named the job contents (recipient address and link).
Over-limit failure row now says the fixed generic text is the only feedback.
DB error row now states the generic error page, that the link stays live and that the user resubmits.
Added a failure row for a failed or lost 'password changed' enqueue after COMMIT.
Notes: explained sessions rows per device and what the worker's retry and drop does.
Added an Open questions section for the breached-list location and email uniqueness.
Submit flow now checks the token first (plain SELECT) before validating the password, so a dead link shows the expired page, not a password error; renumbered steps 1-5 and the DB error row to step 3.
Stated that RAW is a hidden form field and the POST carries it in the body, not the URL.
Added that the rate-limit count includes used and superseded rows, and why.
Expanded the enqueue-fails row to say what the user has and how they recover under the 3/hour limit.
Added that the response is the same status and body every time and that display is a UI choice.
Added that the reset pages need no login and that a logged-out device must log in again.
Specified the periodic delete (rows older than 1 day, any scheduler) and added the scheduler as an open question.
Reordered for a newcomer: summary first, then terms, then data, then the diagram, then notes, then open questions.
Moved the Data section out of the middle and merged the rate-limit and live-link definitions into Terms and Data, so the live-link test is stated once.
Folded the 'link' term and APP_BASE_URL into Terms and added a 'dead' term to cover used and superseded, replacing the phrase 'superseded' in most places with 'replaced'.

Redrew the request flow as numbered steps inside the diagram, removing the stray connector lines and the duplicated 'no user' and 'over limit' routing boxes; failure rows now refer to 'step 8' and 'submit step 3' in plain words.
Removed the UI-choice remark about how the client shows the generic message, and the 'Paths that send nothing' line is kept as one short line.

Merged the 'Rate limit and kill earlier link' and 'Storage' notes: locking is one note, cleanup is another, and the repeated 'rows are kept' and raw-token-storage statements now appear only in Terms and Data.
Merged 'Check on submit' ordering into one 'Order on submit' note and shortened the Logout note.
Dropped the repeated explanation of the enqueue-failure and mail-drop consequences from the notes, leaving it in the failure table and the one 'Silent mail loss' note.
Wrapped the diagram and failure table in a single fenced code block, per the brief; the summary, terms, notes and open questions stay outside it.
holes: Q2: What is the "breached list" and where does it live (local file, table, external service)? How does the server look a password up in it? (author: The brief only says 'the breached-password list' and does not say where it lives or how it is queried. The flow needs only accept/reject, so I added an open question and left the mechanism out.)

Q7: Which email address does the reset link go to, and how is the user looked up (case, whitespace, multiple accounts with the same address)? (author: The link goes to the email on the matched user row. I do not know whether users.email is unique or case-normalised. I decided to trim and lowercase the input and assume uniqueness; recorded as an open question.)

Q13: What does the user see on POST /forgot-password when the email is unknown: is the response truly the same 200 body, and does the client page show it inline or on a new page? (author: The API returns the same 200 status and body in every case. Whether the client shows it inline or on a new page is a UI choice the brief does not specify, so I only noted that it is a UI choice.)

Q15: What is the 'periodic delete' of old rows: what job runs it, how often, and which rows does it remove, given rows are needed for the 1-hour count? (author: I do not know which scheduler exists in the system. I decided the delete removes rows with issued_at older than 1 day, since only the last hour is needed for the count. The scheduler is added to the open questions.)
